Customizing your gaming pc to dominate 4K
240GB SSD in a $5k system? That's just silly. I have a drive that size just for games and I still regularly have to clear out/move games I'm playing less often to make room for new ones.

I have a 240GB SSD for the OS and other various utilities and/or the games I want to load REALLY fast. For all the rest of my games, a couple of 2TB 7200RPM HDDs is more than enough. Load times are still minimal across the board. And I built my PC for under $2K

Load time on a HDD vs a SSD is extremely noticeable in games. I don't see load screens unless the game forces them to show a cutscene/other content. I have no idea why you'd want a fast boot time (OS on SSD) and then sit there forever while your game loads, which you do far more often than reboot your machine. I have everything on SSDs except storage of video and backups which are both too big to be affordable on an SSD.

Anyway, you built your system for 2k. At that budget, I can understand having to go with a smaller SSD. At 5k it's just ridiculous to only have one or to go with a 240GB model. I can't link it because amazon is banned, but there's an $86 difference between the 240 and the 512SSD. On a 5k build, that's not much.

Like I said, load times are still minimal. I also generally prefer having a system that boots quickly and takes a little extra time loading while playing a game because that's more time to get up and stretch/go to the bathroom/whatever.

Plus, lots of games these days are moving to a handful of very large areas that have a common resource set, so seeing loading screens is becoming rarer.

Review: Enter the Gungeon - Super Bunnyhop

A review that criticizes the roguelite genre more than the game's execution of it. Not that there is no merit in discussing this, it's still a bit misleading to do it in the review of a specific game.

I'm not quite sure about that. It may not be fair to compare it to the best (Isaac), but doing so definitely shows me the issue with the early luck and spawns. Isaac does things like give you the first item for free (no key required), compound 'items' a lot more, since many just modify your stats, unlike Gungeon where guns are separate (although there's still passive items, there's just less), and the higher difficulty of Gungeon makes it a lot more noticeable makes shitty item spawns are a lot more punishing. It's understandable if you're trying to do challenges of sorts, but just going normally through the game shouldn't require you to restart runs so much. Isaac also has the fact that when you get lucky, you can be REALLY fucking strong early on, even compared to bosses.

In fact, looking at my list of rogue lites (I'm a fan of the genre), pretty much all of the good ones similarly share the fact that, at least early on, they're easy enough to manage no problem with shitty or no items at all. Crypt of the Necrodancer is a lot more strategy than anything. Isaac the first few bosses (aside maybe the Haunt, fuck that guy) are a walk in the park, Leap of Fate (which I've been playing recently as well) usually leaves you enough room to manage (although it has been unfair at times), Nuclear Throne the bosses are also not too difficult (you'd have to have a lot of bad luck even with just normal items to not get past the first boss), Rogue Legacy comes close, I guess, but at least it doesn't stop your progress with bosses, so you can strengthen yourself before fighting them, in Ziggurat at least the first boss is easy enough.

Other issues aren't as bad, it's basically just that. It needed a bit more ramp up.

Actually I would argue that Isaac is more luck-dependent than Gungeon. In Isaac my personal experience is that if I make it past Mom within a reasonable time frame, there's a very high chance I'll beat the game, even if I'm targeting Hush or Mega Satan. Reason being, either I got super powerful by the time I reached Mom or I didn't. The abundance of items and synergies in Isaac mean that you need at least some of your drops to be good to stand a chance. In Gungeon, the starter weapons are weak, but not horribly gimped compared to what you'll drop most of the time. Furthermore in Isaac it happens quite often that I find myself locked out of most of the good stuff in a level because I don't have enough keys or bombs. In Gungeon, a key is a key, and you don't get more keys by using keys, there's a lot less snowballing.

These days I rarely lose games of Isaac, but that's after more than 200 hours sunk into it. I used to suck big time, and I have no illusion that at least the first few levels in Enter the Gungeon will eventually be a breeze. Not necessarily out of having encyclopedic knowledge of the items but rather mastering the shot patterns and dodge timing.

Anyway, that's a lot of digressing. My point is that in other representatives of this genre, the unbalanced and random nature of the items that you get at the beginning comes with the territory. And I personally like it, because it makes the experience more varied.
